properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 6:58AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A series of fronts are expected to move across the Interior on
Sunday and Monday. The initial front on Sunday will bring a band
of snowfall across the area. With this first front, light snow
accumulations are expected.

The next front moving across the Interior on Monday will be
accompanied by warmer temperatures, which could bring the
potential for a light rain/snow mix in the valleys and moderate
snow amounts across higher elevations. This could lead to slick
travel conditions, especially during the overnight hours Monday
night into Tuesday when the temperatures could drop below freezing
once again.

Accompanying the second front will be a period of gusty winds
across the higher elevations. This could bring some blowing snow
concerns Monday night/Tuesday morning, which could reduce
visibility to one mile or less.

Stay up to date with the latest forecast by visiting our website,
weather.gov/afg.

NWSheadline: ADDITIONAL RAIN AND SNOW COULD BRING DIFFICULT TRAVEL CONDITIONS EARLY NEXT WEEK

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 10:26AM AST until October 26 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE... Across the northern coastal areas including western
and eastern coastal areas.

* WHEN...Remains through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE SUNDAY NIGHT

properties.areaDesc: Shishmaref
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 5:30AM AKDT until October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding is
possible with water levels between 2 to 4 feet above the normal
high tide line. For the High Surf Advisory, water levels
between 1 to 3 ft above the normal high tide line. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, more significant coastal flooding possible
around Monday night. Water Levels between 4 and 6 feet are
possible.

* WHERE...Shishmaref.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM AKDT
Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 PM Sunday to 4 AM
AKDT Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday
night through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding is possible. Some shoreline
erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels up to 4 feet in Shishmaref
may result in erosion on the road to the landfill with high
water in the lagoon.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Precautions should be taken to protect property.
